wwo.name: Jersey City
wwo.method: Harrison street and land traces connect Paulus Hook and Hamilton Park through Van Vorst to Bergen. The 1895 Erie plan corroborates the Pavonia passenger house and ferry approach. Dated inventory entries and surviving parcel frontages anchor three Belmont and Bentley rows. A locally registered 1900 USGS quadrangle supplies the West Bergen street extent, tidal meadow, Hackensack river banks, Communipaw Avenue and Newark & New York Railroad formation to the port. Hudson County records identify the Newark Plank Road bridge and distinguish it from the adjacent canal and southern railway bridge. NJ Transit records identify the 1869 cut through Bergen Hill. Roofs, widths, paving and ground finishes are interpreted. The plan represents the cut as a placement exclusion and the railway as land formations. Track structure, the railway bridge and historical height profiles require separate geometry.

registration.model: Affine pixel to WGS84 fitted in the east crop
registration.limits: Residuals apply around Paulus Hook and Hamilton Park only. The central and Bergen crops share the same 1894 sheet with an exact image-space offset. The 1895 terminal plan corroborates facility use and existing construction. Its image is not a second geodetic fit.

bergen_independent_controls.reference: NJ Office of GIS surviving street intersections matched to the Harrison Bergen crop. Modern streets were not copied into the historic plan.
